body.statement: For each fixed \(c>0\) and \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\), the nonempty fiber \(\{\Delta:(\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_v(P)\}\) is an interval whose infimum and supremum equal the optimal values of the two linear semidefinite programs over \(\mathcal F_c^v(P,\Delta)\). Endpoint inclusion is equivalent to the separate feasibility tests in \(\mathrm{def{:}endpoint\text{-}attainment\text{-}test}\); neither inclusion is inferred from closed PSD constraints alone.
body.justification: Direct all-laws exactness makes both SDP values sharp for every nonempty fixed-slope fiber, including boundary laws.
body.gap: A finite sharp endpoint value may fail to be attained; lower and upper inclusion require separate feasibility tests.
body.consumer: Applied reports can distinguish endpoint values from endpoint membership and compare them with the universal envelope.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(c>0\), \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\), and any \(P\in\Delta^{15}\) for which
\[
 I_v(P,c)=\{d:(\log c,d)\in\Theta_v(P)\}
\]
is nonempty.  No cellwise-positivity condition is imposed.  Write \(z_{\mathrm w}=(m,a,b)\), \(z_+=(m,a,b,t)\), and
\[
 \mathcal G_v(P,c)=\{(z_v,d):z_v\in\mathcal F_c^v(P,d)\}. \tag{1}
\]
For fixed \((P,c)\), every entry of \(H_s\), \(K_s\), and, when \(v=+\), \(R_s\), is affine in \(z_v\); the cell restrictions are affine equalities; and the APE equality is
\[
 d=\sum_{s\in S}L_{m_s}(N_c). \tag{2}
\]
If \(M_0,M_1\succeq0\) and \(0\le\lambda\le1\), then for every conformable vector \(q\),
\[
 q^{\mathsf T}\{\lambda M_0+(1-\lambda)M_1\}q
 =\lambda q^{\mathsf T}M_0q+(1-\lambda)q^{\mathsf T}M_1q\ge0. \tag{3}
\]
Hence every PSD constraint is convex, \(\mathcal G_v(P,c)\) is convex, and its linear projection onto the \(d\)-coordinate is an interval.  By \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}feedback\text{-}cone\text{-}all\text{-}laws}\), that projection is exactly \(I_v(P,c)\), including when \(P\) has zero cells.

The universal geometry in \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}slope\text{-}ape\text{-}envelope}\) gives
\[
 I_v(P,c)\subseteq
 \begin{cases}
 (0,(\sqrt c-1)/(\sqrt c+1)],&c>1,\\
 [-(1-\sqrt c)/(1+\sqrt c),0),&0<c<1,\\
 \{0\},&c=1.
 \end{cases} \tag{4}
\]
For this fixed \(P\), (4) is an outer containment; its sharpness is universal across varying admissible laws, not an assertion that either endpoint is attained at this \(P\).  In particular, the nonempty interval \(I_v(P,c)\) is bounded and has finite infimum and supremum.

The two explicit programs are
\[
 \underline V_v(P,c)=\inf_{d,z_v}\{d:z_v\in\mathcal F_c^v(P,d)\},
 \qquad
 \overline V_v(P,c)=\sup_{d,z_v}\{d:z_v\in\mathcal F_c^v(P,d)\}. \tag{5}
\]
Their objectives are linear, their equality constraints are affine, and their matrix inequalities are affine PSD constraints.  They are therefore linear semidefinite programs.  Exactness gives
\[
 \underline V_v(P,c)=\inf I_v(P,c)=L_c^v(P),
 \qquad
 \overline V_v(P,c)=\sup I_v(P,c)=U_c^v(P). \tag{6}
\]
These are sharp values for the independently defined legal fiber, even if an optimum is not attained.

For the lower value, the all-laws equivalence at \(d=L_c^v(P)\) gives
\[
 L_c^v(P)\in I_v(P,c)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \mathcal F_c^v(P,L_c^v(P))\ne\varnothing. \tag{7}
\]
Similarly,
\[
 U_c^v(P)\in I_v(P,c)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \mathcal F_c^v(P,U_c^v(P))\ne\varnothing. \tag{8}
\]
These are exactly the two separate tests in \(\mathrm{def{:}endpoint\text{-}attainment\text{-}test}\).

Closedness of the matrix cones alone cannot replace (7)--(8), because a linear projection of a closed spectrahedron need not be closed.  For example,
\[
 \mathcal C=\left\{(x,y):
 \begin{bmatrix}x&1\\1&y\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\right\}
\]
is closed, while its projection onto the \(x\)-coordinate is \((0,\infty)\): the PSD condition is equivalent to \(x\ge0\), \(y\ge0\), and \(xy\ge1\).  Thus neither endpoint inclusion follows from closed PSD constraints alone.  Equations (1)--(8) prove the theorem for every nonempty fixed-slope fiber, including boundary observed laws.
